label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service (Towson): Stenvale Aria 3 recalibration, Oct 19 to 27

Last October Dana asked on the General board whether anyone had used Harbor Point, and I said I would write this up once my machine had been through a real trial. It has now been through eight days of trial work, so here is the review.

Equipment: Stenvale Aria 3, my own machine. Harbor Point work order HP-4471.

Dropped off: Monday, October 19. Returned: Tuesday, October 27. That is six business days against the ten they quoted.

Quoted: $285.00 estimate for full keyboard recalibration, number bar depression sensor replacement, internal cleaning, and firmware update (4.0.7 to 4.2.1).

Paid: $310.00 total. That is the $285.00 plus $25.00 for an internal battery replacement. The battery was holding about 60% of its rated capacity. Gloria emailed me the price and did not proceed until I approved it in writing. That mattered to me, and I would expect any shop to do the same. I paid by card at pickup. I paid personally and was not reimbursed by anyone.

Loaner: yes, a Stenvale Aria 2 was issued while mine was in the shop. Its tilt arm would not hold its position, and it slipped mid-afternoon on a working day, so I had to prop it on a legal pad for the rest of that day. I told Gloria in writing, and she thanked me and said they would repair the arm. That is a problem with the loaner, not the service on my machine, but it is fair to mention.

Phone access: this is the real weakness. The phone line is staffed Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4, and only then. On Wednesday, October 21, I called to ask about progress and the line rang out with no voicemail set up. Gloria emailed me the next day. If you work a Monday docket, or you need to reach them outside those hours, plan on email, and build in extra time.

The work: the machine came back with a printed one-page service sheet listing every adjustment made. I have never had that from a repair shop before, and it is what I most wanted to see. The first full day back was expert testimony, an engineer who talks in numbers, and the number bar did not double a single stroke. The work carries a 90-day warranty.

Verdict: $310 was fair for what was done. The work was careful, the paperwork was clear, and the turnaround came in under the quote. The phone hours are the thing to plan around. Dana, if you want someone who does careful work on a Stenvale and tells you exactly what they changed, I would trust them with your Aria. Just plan around the phone.

reasons: The draft says sensor replacement was included in the original estimate, but the work order specified sensor inspection.
